finding_note: The provided San Diego city documents do not enact or propose a city rent cap or rent-control formula. D073 §98.0705 only requires a notice stating, "California law limits the amount your rent can be increased. See California Civil Code section 1947.12 for more information," which describes state law rather than a San Diego-enacted rent increase limit, so it is not reportable as this jurisdiction's rule for this category. D076/S012 concern algorithmic rent-setting software, not rent increase caps. No failed or pending San Diego rent-control measure appears in these documents.

rules.title: Residential Tenant Protections just-cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: San Diego requires just cause to terminate a tenancy in covered residential rental property, defines at-fault and no-fault just causes, requires specified notices to tenants and the Housing Commission, and requires relocation assistance for no-fault terminations. Covered tenants may also have a right of first offer to re-rent within five years after certain no-fault evictions, and noncompliance can void the termination notice.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; no-fault relocation assistance = 2 months' actual rent, or 3 months' actual rent if tenant is a senior or disabled

from the title to any other dwelling unit, provided that both of the following

rules.penalty: A tenant may seek injunctive relief, equitable relief, and money damages, including punitive damages; wrongful eviction damages are not less than three times actual economic damages; failure to provide required relocation assistance makes the landlord liable for not less than three times the required relocation assistance and actual economic damages; the City may enforce with civil and criminal remedies.
rules.rule_quote: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.interaction_text:

rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination and income-standard restrictions
rules.requirement: San Diego prohibits refusing to rent, renew, or continue a tenancy, advertising discrimination, or imposing tenancy terms based on a person's source of income, and it bars financial or income standards that fail to count the tenant's full lawful income or qualifying assistance. Owner-occupied shared kitchen/bathroom arrangements are exempt.
rules.key_value: Must account for tenant's entire source of income; may not discriminate based on source of income

rules.penalty: Aggrieved person may seek an injunction; court may award monetary damages, including three times one month's rent for violations during or before tenancy, plus punitive damages, attorneys’ fees, and costs.
rules.rule_quote:
It is unlawful for any person to use a financial or income standard for
                           entering into or renewing a tenancy that does either of the following:

                           (1)    Fails to account for any tenant’s or prospective tenant’s entire
                                  source of income; or

                           (2)    Fails to account for the aggregate source of income of tenants
                                  residing together or proposing to reside together, or the aggregate
                                  source of income of tenants or prospective tenants and their
                                  cosigners or proposed cosigners, on the same basis as the
                                  aggregate source of income of married persons residing together or

rules.title: San Diego ban on anti-competitive automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: San Diego prohibits selling, licensing, or otherwise providing an algorithmic device to a landlord, and prohibits landlords from using an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. Covered algorithmic devices use or incorporate algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels; specified reporting, affordable-housing, and appraisal tools are excluded.
rules.key_value: Use or sale of covered algorithmic devices prohibited; tenant may recover up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each residential rental property can be a separate violation

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
coverage_conditions.quote: Residential rental property has the same meaning as in San Diego Municipal Code section 98.0702, as may be amended.

coverage_conditions.value: algorithmic device using nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords
coverage_conditions.text: Covered software must use or incorporate algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels.
coverage_conditions.quote:
Algorithmic device means a software or product that uses or incorporates one or more
               algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data of two or more
               landlords to advise a landlord on, or recommend to a landlord, rental rates or
               occupancy levels that may be achieved for a residential rental property in the City of
               San Diego.

exemptions.text: Excluded are tools that publish reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or public information and do not recommend future rental rates or occupancy levels.
exemptions.quote:
(a)    A software or product used by a person to publish reports regarding rental
                      rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor
                      data that is more than 90 days old, or from information available to the
                      general public, and does not recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for
                      future residential rental property leases or renewals.

exemptions.text: Excluded are tools used to establish rental rates or income limits under local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
exemptions.quote:
(b)    A software or product used by a person to establish rental rates or income
                      limits in accordance with local, state, or federal affordable housing program
                      guidelines.

exemptions.value: appraisal software without runtime rent recommendations
exemptions.text: Excluded are appraisal tools that do not recommend rental rates during runtime operation.
exemptions.quote:
(c)    A software or product used by a person conducting an appraisal that does not
                      recommend rental rates during the runtime operation of the software or
                      product.

rules.penalty: A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; a prevailing landlord or tenant shall recover costs and reasonable attorney’s fees; the City may enforce the Division, including civil and criminal remedies.
rules.rule_quote:
(a)    It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic
                            device to a landlord.

                     (b)    It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or
                            occupancy levels for residential rental property.

                            For each month a violation of section 98.1103(b) exists or continues, and for
                            each residential rental property a landlord uses an algorithmic device, it shall
                            constitute a separate and distinct violation.
rules.interaction_text:
(b)    The remedies under section 98.1104 are cumulative and are in addition to any
                      other remedies in this Division or at law, statute, or ordinance.

rules.title: Proposed San Diego anti-competitive automated rent price-fixing ordinance
rules.requirement: The proposed ordinance would have added Division 11 to prohibit selling, licensing, or otherwise providing an algorithmic device to a landlord, and to prohibit landlords from using an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. The proposal defined covered algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data concerning rental rates, occupancy levels, or other leasing information, with exclusions for certain reporting and affordable-housing tools, and would have allowed tenant civil actions for up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: Proposed ban on use or sale of covered algorithmic devices; proposed tenant remedy up to $1,000 per violation

rules.rule_quote:
§98.1103  Use and Sale of Algorithmic Devices Prohibited
(a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an
algorithmic device to a landlord.
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
For each month a violation of section 98.1103(b) exists or continues, and
for each residential rental property a landlord uses an algorithmic device,
it shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.
rules.interaction_text:
(b) The remedies under section 98.1104 are cumulative and are in addition to
any other remedies in this Division or at law, statute, or ordinance.
